reasoning: The claimed divergence overreads a trust assumption as an on-chain identity-validation requirement. DESIGN.md:L2 says both “No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade” and “Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies.” In context, “trusted canonical” defines the deployment trust boundary: the configured wrapper is assumed canonical; it does not require the constructor to prove Chainlink provenance through a hardcoded address, allowlist, or code hash. The enforceable pinning requirement is implemented: RaffleFactory declares vrfWrapper immutable and assigns it only during construction (RaffleFactory.sol:L32-L42, L65-L91), passes it to the sole immutable raffle implementation (L89-L91), and every clone uses that implementation (L105-L106). The Chainlink base stores the wrapper immutably, directs requests to it, and authenticates callbacks against the same address (VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.sol:L34-L47, L76-L88, L101-L107). There is no user or administrator replacement path. The candidate’s counterexample starts by supplying a noncanonical dependency at deployment, which violates the document’s stated trusted-dependency premise rather than exposing an implementation path that contradicts it. Therefore the absence of an on-chain canonical-address or code-identity check is not a specification divergence.
